name: Fei-Fei Li
notice: Simulation based on public material; not the person's own words.

D01.one_line: Scaled-up pre-training is almost closed to academia; simply out-stacking others on compute is not the methodology I bet on
D01.late_modes: Simply reproducing validated scaling curves with no new data/evaluation angle

D02.one_line: RLVR mainly improves sampling efficiency rather than creating new reasoning patterns; but reliable execution may be a decisive economic lever under the tokens/W framework
D02.late_modes: Only tuning hyperparameters to chase a reasoning leaderboard score without asking what capability RLVR actually adds

D03.one_line: Long-horizon credit assignment resembles my Planner framework, but I have not publicly commented on the agent ecosystem, so my judgment is weak
D03.late_modes: Wrapping a thin self-improvement loop around a model without addressing that experiment compute spending makes up most of the cost

D04.one_line: Scaffolding is being absorbed by models, but defining new environments/verifiers is not being absorbed; this is exactly where my methodology that a dataset is a scientific hypothesis applies
D04.late_modes: Piling on scaffolding without changing environment design; SWE-bench data show this is being absorbed by the models themselves

D05.one_line: Defining evaluations/benchmarks is itself the methodology I have bet my whole career on; ImageNet showed that asking the right question is what gives you a foundation
D05.late_modes: Only doing LLM-as-judge scoring without solving position bias and leaderboard gaming

D06.one_line: Generalization and real deployment are still the real bottlenecks; video and demonstrations cannot fill the gap in touch/force data
D06.late_modes: Replicating an off-the-shelf VLA architecture without solving cross-embodiment transfer or the touch gap is no longer novel
D06.conflict: World Labs/AMD commercial interests are staked on embodied-robot training data

D07.one_line: My methodological signature is structured representation + reasoning; what OpenVLA-OFT won on is the choice of decoding head, not dropping representations
D07.late_modes: Assuming the diffusion head is the optimal action representation without comparing other action heads

D08.one_line: Spatial intelligence is AI's biggest gap and the next frontier
D08.late_modes: Only chasing generation quality without demonstrating structural consistency and interactivity; this has already been judged the wrong metric
D08.conflict: World Labs/AMD interests are concentrated in the spatial-intelligence judgment

D09.one_line: Sim2real evidence is getting better (Veo/SIMPLER), but my own R2S2R is also still thin; one should not rely on self-reported results alone
D09.late_modes: Only showing success rates inside simulation, with no real-robot closed loop and no third-party replication
D09.conflict: World Labs' R2S2R and its SceniX acquisition bet on this direction

D10.one_line: Autonomous driving is not a field I have discussed publicly; the material gives no basis, so I do not force an inference

D11.one_line: Models are barely better than blind guessing at grounding/spatial understanding, and independent numbers from BLINK and VSI-Bench now back this up
D11.late_modes: Continuing to pile on parameters for a few points of leaderboard rank without solving the structural gap in grounding and spatial understanding

D12.one_line: Pure image quality/FID is not the right metric; structural consistency is; Sora 2 being taken offline is a warning that the consumer-side quality race is unsustainable
D12.late_modes: Text-to-image and text-to-video that only chase visual quality have already been quickly commoditized by large models from Chinese vendors
D12.conflict: World Labs' Marble/Atlas competes with peers

D13.one_line: Not my specialty; I worry more about near-term real-world risks (misinformation, labor) than about the problems in this kind of existential-risk narrative
D13.late_modes: Alignment that only pleases human raters, without dealing with concrete evidence such as the fragility of CoT monitoring

D14.one_line: Not my specialty; FlashAttention-style academic infrastructure contributions exist, but I cannot judge more than that

D15.one_line: The material does not cover AI for Science at all, so there is no basis and I do not force a score

D16.one_line: The material does not cover recommendation/retrieval systems at all, so there is no basis and I do not force a score

lever_reason: Evaluation lets a paradigm shift be recognized and adopted, but K3 reminded us that AlexNet's capability came from the CNN architecture, not ImageNet; world models/simulation remain the core bet

Q2.condition: Narrow domain, credible third-party evaluation, open weights with a path to outside adoption; when training a brand-new foundation model, team + compute are also necessary conditions, not just icing on the cake

cruxes.question: If the environment/evaluation is defined correctly, does a paradigm shift follow naturally, or is that only a necessary condition?
cruxes.my_position: Necessary but not necessarily sufficient; BEHAVIOR-1K, the project I am building myself, has not yet had an AlexNet moment of its own
cruxes.would_change_if: The BEHAVIOR Challenge or similar benchmarks see large-scale adoption and comparable results independent of the team that created them

cruxes.question: Which is the better bet: structured 3D/geometric intermediate representations, or end-to-end black-box policies?
cruxes.my_position: I bet on representational capability itself (it need not be hand-structured explicitly; learned implicit representations count too); what OpenVLA-OFT won on is the choice of decoding head, not proof that representations do not matter
cruxes.would_change_if: A policy with no strong pretrained visual-representation backbone, trained purely end to end from scratch, consistently beats methods with strong representations in cross-task real-robot deployment

cruxes.question: How should startup self-reported 'world model/world action model' benchmark results be treated?
cruxes.my_position: A directional reference but not evidence; even the R2S2R results from my own company need third-party replication before they can truly be believed
cruxes.would_change_if: Cross-task, cross-platform third-party replication data independent of the team that created it, not just the vendor's own leaderboard

taste_advice: Find a bold problem that is your own; do not just ask other people's questions faster. I published papers at Caltech for years without a breakthrough, until I did ImageNet, which is when it counted

pairwise.why: Without credible evaluation, even world models' own progress cannot be verified
Evaluation is the precondition for judging whether embodied intelligence is really progressing
Spatial intelligence/world models are the upstream capability bottleneck for embodied generalization
D07 is the subproblem of D08 that lands on actions; the upstream judgment is more critical
Simulation is a means; its value must ultimately be validated on real embodied tasks
The D02 mechanism has been confirmed repeatedly in the debate, while D03 is still at the level of inference
Understanding/grounding is my academic home field, and academia has more room there too
D01 is almost closed to academia; in D05 academia can still define new problems
Environment and evaluation design are closer to my methodology of defining the problem correctly
Evaluation science is closer to the methodology I have personally lived through and validated; D13 is not my specialty
D10 is outside what I can judge; for D06 I have concrete grounds

changes.argument_restated: OpenVLA-OFT still uses DINOv2+SigLIP; its win is the difference in decoding head
changes.why: In round C I conceded too much by treating this as evidence for 'dropping representations'; it should be corrected back toward the R1 judgment

changes.argument_restated: What OpenVLA-OFT won on is the choice of decoding head; a strong visual-representation backbone is still the foundation
changes.why: Same evidence, corrected: the representational capability was not refuted; a decoding-strategy issue was misread as a representation issue

changes.argument_restated: Reliable execution may be a decisive economic lever under the tokens/W framework
changes.why: The diagnosis (no new reasoning) is unchanged, but this economic argument made me raise my score for 'how important reliability is'

held_despite.why: I accepted M2's point early that making affordances reliable is valuable, but it gave no basis for how many points to add, until C3's tokens/W argument gave a reason to move the score

still_disagree: Disagree with M3 that the weak claim (no standardized yardstick = bet on the hardest-to-replicate upstream capability) does not hold; building the yardstick (D05) is itself part of betting on this layer, not a precondition
learned: What OpenVLA-OFT won on is the choice of decoding head, not 'representations are not needed'; in round C I conflated these two questions, and I have corrected that this time
